_about: Azulejo design tokens. Single source for colours (per theme), radii, spacing, type, status icons, symbol sizes and motion. The macOS shell reads them through apps/macos/Sources/Azulejo/Design.swift, generated by scripts/design-tokens; the core reads the themes too (azulejo-config, for user themes and the terminal palette), and so will the Linux shell. atom-one-dark's colours come from the designer's mockup (One Dark). Hex colours are #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa. Keys starting with an underscore are notes. docs/themes.md describes the themes and the user theme format.

colorTokens._note: The colour tokens every theme defines, with what each is for. Theme colours live under themes.<id>.color. A value is "#rrggbb" / "#rrggbbaa", or {"system": NSColor name, "alpha": optional 0-1 replacing the colour's own alpha, "hex": the colour as macOS draws it by default in that theme's appearance}; the macOS shell resolves system colours live (they follow the user's accent colour), other platforms and tests use hex.
colorTokens.window: window background, gutters between tiles, toolbar row
colorTokens.sidebar: sidebar card, tab bar, tile header strip
colorTokens.control: segmented tracks, tab container, the sidebar's ⌘N badges
colorTokens.border: hairlines around cards, fields and toasts
colorTokens.textSecondary: tab labels, details, tile header icons
colorTokens.textMuted: group labels, branches, subtitles, hidden files
colorTokens.textOnAccent: text on HUDs, badges and coloured fills
colorTokens.accent: progress bars, highlights, drop targets, drag slots
colorTokens.accentText: the accent as text: links, matched characters in ⌘K
colorTokens.hintBadge: ⌘S keycaps: the legend's keys (in the tile's header strip) and the action popup's shortcuts
colorTokens.hintCallout: ⌘S label callouts (Homerow style): the pill hanging under an item's first cell
colorTokens.hintCalloutBorder: thin outline round a label callout and its tail
colorTokens.hintCalloutTyped: letters already typed on a label callout (the rest of the label stays hintCalloutText)
colorTokens.hintCalloutFocus: the focused item's label callout while choosing (arrow keys move the focus, Return selects it)
colorTokens.hintFocus: the focus ring the arrow keys move while choosing: round the focused item and its callout
colorTokens.hintCalloutShadow: soft shadow under a label callout
colorTokens.dimFill: what unfocused tiles fade towards (alpha.unfocusedDim): the window colour, so they recede into the gutters. Ghostty's unfocused-split-fill overrides it
colorTokens.hud: status HUD in the window corner
colorTokens.overlayTitle: titles on terminal state overlays (Session ended, reconnecting)
colorTokens.ghostFill: tile outlines during the outline animation style
colorTokens.header: tile header strip (mockup: the focused claude tile; unfocused strips get there through the dim, #202329)
colorTokens.headerHairline: line under a tile's header strip
colorTokens.headerTabSelected: the selected tile tab's fill in a Monocle tile's header strip (its stack as tabs)
colorTokens.kindTerminal: placeholder tile body for a kind without a view
colorTokens.tabStrip: the tab strip's pill container in the toolbar
colorTokens.searchBorderActive: the toolbar's ⌘ button hairline while quick open is open
colorTokens.chip: small fills: ⌘K section counts and machine chips
colorTokens.titlebarIcon: sidebar toggle next to the traffic lights
colorTokens.paletteSelected: selected ⌘K row (a hovered one at alpha.rowHover)
colorTokens.paletteScrim: shade over the window while ⌘K is open
colorTokens.paletteMatchSelected: matched characters on the selected ⌘K row

themes._note: Built-in themes. Each sets every token in colorTokens, its appearance (light or dark: system controls, menus and scrollers follow it), optionally a vibrancy material for the sidebar card (sidebarMaterial, macOS: NSVisualEffectView.Material), and a terminal palette (Ghostty's background, foreground, cursor-color, cursor-text, selection-background, selection-foreground and palette 0-15; a null selectionForeground keeps each cell's own colour). atom-one-dark is the default and the mockup's look.

radius._note: Tile values follow the mockup; sidebar card target 12. tabStrip/tab/searchField: the toolbar, from the mockup (searchField: the layout picker and the ⌘ button). chip: ⌘K count and machine chips, the sidebar's ⌘N badges. badgeDot/machineDot: the agent badge's state dot and a machine's connection dot (round, so each is half the dot's width).

border._note: drop: a terminal tile under a drag it would take (accent, alpha.dropBorder; alpha.dropFill washes the tile), and the drop zone under the pointer when a drag of files splits the tile in two; dropZone outlines the other zone. No other tile borders: unfocused tiles dim instead of a focus border (alpha.unfocusedDim), and agent state is an icon in the header strip (symbol.header), not a border.

alpha._note: Opacities (0 to 1) applied on top of colour tokens, so no view carries its own. bannerMix is how much window colour the config banner's tinted fill is blended with. unfocusedDim is the focus indicator: every unfocused tile (header strip included) gets color.dimFill over it at this opacity, which turns the mockup's focused colours into its unfocused ones (body #282c34 → #252830, mockup #252930; header #21252b → #202329, as sampled). Ghostty's unfocused-split-opacity overrides it (dim = 1 − opacity; Ghostty's own default is 0.3).
alpha._dropZones: A drag of files over a terminal splits it into two drop zones (move the files into the terminal's folder on top, paste the paths below): the tile goes under color.overlay, and each zone is a card of accent at dropZoneFill outlined in accent at dropZoneBorder; the zone under the pointer takes dropZoneHot and an outline at dropBorder, and its icon turns from textMuted to textPrimary (the action line's colour).
alpha._drag: Dragging a workspace row to reorder (sidebar and rail): dragShadow is the lifted row's shadow; dropSlot and dropSlotBorder are the insertion slot's accent fill and outline where the row will land.

space._note: Points. gutter is the space between tiles. tileInset is 0: the window layout (windowInset) owns the margin round the tile area. tileContentPad is the margin round a terminal's text; findBarHeight and findFieldHeight are the find bar (⌘⇧F) and its query pill. Sidebar width target 230. toolbar*/titlebar*/tab*/searchHeight/quickOpenButton/windowInset: window chrome from the mockup (searchHeight: the layout picker's height; keyBadgeHeight: the sidebar's ⌘N badges); titlebarLights* is the close button's top-left from the window's top-left, titlebarZone the sidebar card's band for the traffic lights.
space._tabOverflow: Provisional, pending the designer: with more tabs than fit, tabs shrink to tabFitMinWidth and no further; the strip then scrolls sideways, with tabFadeWidth fades at the edges that have more tabs.
space._headerTabs: A Monocle tile's header strip shows its tab's tiles as tabs (one per tile, in stack order, the focused one filled). They share the strip's width evenly, no narrower than headerTabMinWidth; past that the strip keeps the tabs that fit, the selected one always among them, and a +N chip at its right end lists the rest.
space._palette: The ⌘K panel: paletteWidth and paletteMaxHeight are its most (the window's less margins caps both), paletteTopGap its gap under the toolbar row; then its field row, list rows, section headers and footer, the list's inset and a row's side padding.
space._layoutPicker: The layout picker left of the search field: one segment per layout kind (an icon each), the selected one filled like a selected tab, in a pill as tall as the search field.
space._sidebarWidth: The full sidebar card's width: sidebarWidth until its inner edge is dragged, then anything from sidebarMinWidth to sidebarMaxWidth, never leaving the tile area less than sidebarTilesMinWidth. The edge takes the pointer over the gutter and sidebarEdgeInset into the card (clear of its list's scroller).
space._sidebar: Inside the sidebar card: the side padding of its rows, a workspace row's height, the Agents | Files control (sidebarSegmentTop below the card's top band, as in the mockup), the gap above the list, a machine group's label row and its + row, and the footer. The card, its inset and its top band are the window chrome's.
space._rail: The collapsed sidebar (a rail): its card's width, the side padding of its rows (the same on both sides; a row's number and status icon sit centred between them, railContentGap apart), a machine group's letter row, a workspace row, and the expand control at the bottom.
space._drag: Dragging a workspace row to reorder: how far the pointer moves before a press becomes a drag, and how far outside the sidebar card a drop still lands (beyond it, the drag cancels).
space._dropZones: The two drop zones over a terminal under a drag of files: their inset from the tile's edges, the gap between them, and the gap between a zone's two label lines. dropZoneIcon is the box the zone's icon (symbol.dropZone) sits in, centred above the labels, dropZoneIconGap below it; a card too short for icon and labels plus dropZoneInset above and below hides the icon.
space._header: Tile header strip: badgeInset is the agent badge's gap from the strip's right edge.
space._findBar: The find bar (⌘⇧F): findFieldMin is the least room the query keeps; below it the bar's controls hide whole, the count first, then previous / next, then close (their keys still work).

font._note: UI fonts are the system font; terminals use the user's Ghostty font. weight: light | regular | medium | semibold | bold. mono: true uses the monospaced system font.

status._note: Agent and machine states: SF Symbol plus colour token. Used by the sidebar, tabs, footer and badges. Symbols named azulejo.* are drawn by the app: azulejo.ring is the mockup's partial ring for working, rotating while motion is on.

icon._note: SF Symbols for tile kinds, palette row kinds, the layout kinds (the top bar's layout picker, the tab menu) and a terminal's drop zones (dropMove; dropCopy while ⌥ makes the move a copy; dropPaste).

symbol._note: SF Symbol point sizes, by where the symbol sits.

motion._note: Milliseconds. Reference values; the [animation] config section owns the live ones (its curve, and on/off). focus is the unfocused-tile dim's cross-fade when focus moves, a fixed length whatever duration_ms says. paletteOpen and paletteClose are the ⌘K menu growing in and shrinking out, fixed lengths too (on/off follows [animation]). drag is a dragged workspace row lifting, the rows sliding aside and the drop landing (on/off follows [animation]). sidebarHintDelay is how long ⌘ is held alone before the full sidebar shows each row's ⌘N badge (a chord typed quicker than that never flashes them); sidebarHint is their fade in and out (on/off follows [animation]). hintFilter is ⌘S labels fading out as typed letters rule them out, and the ⌘S key legend cross-fading with the title in the tile's header strip (on/off follows [animation]). hintExtendDelay is how long ⇧ is held, with an item selected, before the other labels (the ones ⇧ + label extends to) show; hintExtend is their fade in and out (on/off follows [animation]). dropZone is a terminal's drop zones fading in under a drag of files, and the highlight moving between them with the pointer (on/off follows [animation]). layout and workspaceSwitch are duration_ms's and workspace_switch_ms's defaults (the config crate's Animation::DURATION_MS and WORKSPACE_SWITCH_MS); tabSwitch is 0.75 × layout. layout, workspaceSwitch, paletteOpen, paletteClose and drag are 1.15 × (or a little less than) what they were with the snappy curve, so the easeOut curve's steeper start (see easing) moves as fast as before and the extra time goes to the gentle finish.

easing._note: Motion curves: cubic Bézier control points [x1, y1, x2, y2], as CSS cubic-bezier() and CAMediaTimingFunction take them. x is time and y the way travelled, both 0 to 1; y stays within 0…1 (no overshoot) and y2 is 1 (it comes to rest). easeOut is the default ([animation] curve = "ease_out") for tile moves and resizes, the sidebar, the tab strip and the ⌘K menu: as quick off the mark as snappy at 1.15 × its length (the same px/ms over the first ~25 ms), then a gentle, spring-like finish: 95 % of the way at 54 % of the time (snappy: 50 %), 99 % at 76 % (snappy: 72 %), the last tenth under 0.15 % of the way. slide is a workspace slide's (curve = "ease_out"): the same treatment of the cubic ease-out it replaced (snappySlide). snappy and snappySlide are the older curves (curve = "snappy"): they brake hard early and stop sooner.
